data.body:
Fix pushed for review: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1493

Confirmed the root cause before editing rather than taking the report on faith. `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` uploads a PEP 740 bundle carrying the `https://docs.pypi.org/attestations/publish/v1` predicate to **PyPI's** attestation store; `gh attestation verify --repo` reads **GitHub's** Artifact Attestations store, which holds SLSA provenance. Different stores, different predicates — the documented command could never have worked, and its failure mode reads as "this release is unattested" rather than "you asked the wrong service", which is the part that makes it a bug rather than a typo.

Changes:
- `docs/releasing.md`: the consumer recipe is now `pypi-attestations verify pypi --repository https://github.com/navapbc/rebar pypi:nava_rebar-X.Y.Z-py3-none-any.whl` (the official verifier, per pypi/pypi-attestations), plus a callout keeping the two stores distinct and recording the 0.11.0 evidence. GitHub's immutable-release attestation is preserved as the separate guarantee it is.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: the `attestations: true` comment now names the PyPI store, the predicate URL, and the correct consumer verifier. No publish-behaviour change.
- `tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py`: four cells pinning the documented command, the `--repository` identity, the predicate URL, and the workflow comment.

One design note on the negative assertion: the obvious form (`"gh attestation verify" not in doc`) would forbid the prose that explains WHY the GitHub verifier is wrong — the most valuable sentence in the section. So it parses the fenced code blocks and asserts none of them offers that command as a runnable recipe. Prose about the wrong store stays allowed, and wanted.
